attestation.note: Source-map paraphrase, not a verbatim transcription: Theorem 1 supplies preservation under a covered reversal and Theorem 2 supplies the finite sequence of distinct disagreement-reducing covered reversals.

added_lemmas.statement: For proper blocked edge-coloured directed acyclic graphs, in which every edge-colour block has at least two members, equality of the associated linear Gaussian covariance models implies equality of the coloured directed acyclic graphs.

attestation.note: Source-map paraphrase of the proper BPEC structural-identifiability implication used only to identify the endpoint reduction with the published result.

proposed_statement_changes.reason: The frozen equality is ill typed because the reversal component is a set of blocked states whereas an ordinary Markov-equivalence class is a set of directed acyclic graphs.  The proposed statement gives the exact graph-projection bijection and its unique singleton lift; it preserves the intended mathematical conclusion while removing the type ambiguity.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The proof uses the published covered-reversal sequence at theorem granularity, so the cited leaf must be an explicit dependency.

proposed.justification: The theorem converts the observable separator into both a static criterion and a complete local transformation calculus.
proposed.gap: BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026, Question 20, asks for graphical edge-coloured equivalence and Theorem 19 excludes singleton classes; Chickering1995, Theorem 2, permits every covered reversal and has no coefficient-partition legality condition.
proposed.consumer: Singleton-permitting causal-community discovery can report the exact observational component rather than either forcing proper colours or claiming a unique DAG.

proposed.gap: Chickering1995 and BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026 establish the two endpoints separately but do not characterize the singleton-permitting interpolation.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The proof directly uses covariance-model equality for every selected-component member and the off-model regression recovery map, so those nodes are made explicit dependencies.

proposed.justification: The observationally recovered object is a finite set of member-labelled causal effects, so inference must cover every component member.
proposed.gap: NandyMaathuisRichardson2017 derives joint effect inference across ordinary equivalence classes, and StriederDrton2023 uses test inversion under equal variances; neither treats equality-constrained coefficient blocks after exact blocked-component selection.
proposed.consumer: A causal-community analysis can report simultaneous uncertainty for all total effects compatible with its recovered singleton-permitting component.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The exact Pareto frontier of the maximum active-block count and maximum rational height for universal separator schemes remains undetermined.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen handle does not define the admissible scheme class, normalization of polynomial certificates, or which numerical objects contribute to height.  Without those choices, rescaling a certificate changes its recorded height and unrestricted non-star source parameters make active-block support incomparable, so a universal lower-bound statement is not well typed.  Even after restricting to unit-noise rational source covariances and the two frozen certificate formats, proving that one active block or a smaller height cannot separate all unequal signatures requires a new crossing-partition lower-bound construction not supplied by the core.
open_obligations.attempted: I reduced the support lower bound to the empty-graph versus one-edge pair and examined the crossing-partition and unequal-family reversed-edge cases used by the upper router.  They prove necessity of some nonzero activation but do not rule out a different one-block covariance or a lower-height nonbinary choice.
